chunks: From him, from Faḍālah, from Abī al-Miʿzā, who said:
I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a pregnant woman whose pregnancy has become apparent, and who sees blood as a menstruating woman sees.

He عليه السلام said: "That is bleeding. If it is abundant blood, then she should not perform salat (prayer); and if it is little, then she should perform ghusl (ritual bath) at the time of every two prayers."

key_terms.فَلْتَغْتَسِلْ: then she should perform ghusl (ritual bath)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a pregnant woman who sees blood in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning a pregnant woman who experiences bleeding. Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام distinguishes between heavy and light bleeding, assigning different rulings for salat (prayer) and ghusl (ritual bath) accordingly. It is significant in Shia fiqh discussions on ḥayḍ, istiḥāḍah, and related rulings of ritual purity.
